correctness.evidence: Independently re-ran bazel test //tests:test_gate //tests:test_task: test_gate 20/20, test_task 180/180 (previously 16/20 and 176/180). Confirmed the __main__ blocks in both files now sit after every test class, matching the accepted plan; no assertion or behavior changes, scope limited to tests/test_gate.py, tests/test_task.py, CHANGELOG.md, and no other test_*.py file has the same shape.

correctness-tests-specialist independently reproduced bazel test //tests:test_gate //tests:test_task (20/20, 180/180) and confirmed the reordering is byte-identical apart from position (AST scan: no class follows either __main__ guard, no assertions changed).

error_handling.evidence: No error-handling paths were modified; the newly-executing test classes include real error-path assertions (e.g. test_gate.py's out-of-repo target returning 'ask') that previously never ran.

test_quality.evidence: correctness-tests-specialist found tests/test_verify_release.py has no __main__ guard and runs 0/13 tests under Bazel (same defect class, in-scope per the PR's own CHANGELOG completeness claim), plus no regression guard exists to catch this defect class if reintroduced. See findings outer-r7-verify-release-main-block (blocking) and outer-r7-no-regression-guard (non-blocking).

findings.summary: tests/test_verify_release.py has no `if __name__ == "__main__"` block at all, so Bazel runs it as __main__ and unittest.main() is never called: ReleaseVerificationTests (8) and BundlePackagingTests (5) all run 0/13 under Bazel, while `python -m unittest` runs all 13. This is the same silent-skip defect class this PR exists to fix, and it falls inside the PR's own stated scope -- the CHANGELOG claims 'every test module was scanned for the same shape,' which is true only for the 'class below the guard' shape and misses the 'no guard at all' sibling shape.

No regression guard exists to fail if a __main__-block-placement or missing-__main__ defect is reintroduced in any tests/test_*.py file; the failure mode is silent by construction (CI's `python -m unittest discover` legs stay green either way). Suggested follow-up: a small AST-based meta-test asserting every tests/test_*.py ends with an `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` guard as its last top-level statement, following the precedent of tests/test_documentation_links.py, tests/test_permission_surface.py, and tests/test_navigator_coverage.py.

evidence.delivered: Added the missing if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main() block to tests/test_verify_release.py (was missing entirely, so Bazel ran 0/13 of its tests) and added tests/test_every_test_class_runs_under_bazel.py, an AST-based regression guard that fails if any tests/test_*.py file is ever missing a trailing __main__ guard.
evidence.deviations: None beyond the scope of the triaged finding (outer-r7-verify-release-main-block) and the accompanying non-blocking suggestion (outer-r7-no-regression-guard), both of which the developer explicitly authorized addressing in this same round.
validation: ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy on both changed/new files -> clean

test_quality.evidence: correctness-tests-specialist re-verified only the triaged correction: confirmed tests/test_verify_release.py now ends with the __main__ guard after every class; empirically ran the new AST helper against the actual pre-fix (eba8ea2^) file contents and confirmed it flags both the misplaced-guard shape (test_gate.py, test_task.py) and the missing-guard shape (test_verify_release.py); reproduced bazel test //tests:test_verify_release (13/13, was 0/13) and //tests:test_every_test_class_runs_under_bazel (1/1); confirmed the CHANGELOG's inaccurate completeness claim was corrected. One non-blocking follow-up raised (outer-r9-guard-negative-case): approved with a hardening suggestion, not a defect.

findings.summary: The new regression guard's own detection helper (_last_statement_is_main_guard) is only exercised against the current, already-clean tree, with no inline test of a known-bad input (misplaced guard, or no guard at all). If the helper ever regressed to a vacuous check, this meta-test would stay green while verifying nothing -- the same failure mode the task exists to eliminate. Suggested follow-up: add unit cases that feed the helper three inline source strings (guard last, guard misplaced above a class, no guard) and assert on the result directly.
